title: Writing Equations for Horizontally Shifted Parabolas
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = -x^2 (vertex at the origin, opening downward) is shifted horizontally to two new positions: Position (a) has its vertex at (-7, 0), and Position (b) has its vertex at (4, 0). Write the equation for each new graph.

steps.title: Recall the Horizontal Shift Rule for y = f(x)
steps.mathExpression: y = f(x - h) \text{ shifts the graph right by } h > 0; \quad y = f(x + |h|) \text{ shifts left by } |h|
steps.explanation: Replacing x with x - h translates every point (x, y) on the graph of y = f(x) horizontally to (x + h, y).
steps.why: Horizontal translation of a function graph by h units replaces x with x - h.

steps.title: Write the Equation for Position (a)
steps.explanation: Position (a) shifts the vertex of y = -x^2 from (0, 0) to (-7, 0), which is a shift of 7 units to the left (h = -7). Replacing x with x + 7 gives y = -(x + 7)^2.
steps.why: Setting x = -7 in y = -(x + 7)^2 yields the maximum value y = 0 at the shifted vertex (-7, 0).

steps.title: Write the Equation for Position (b)
steps.explanation: Position (b) shifts the vertex from (0, 0) to (4, 0), which is a shift of 4 units to the right (h = 4). Replacing x with x - 4 gives y = -(x - 4)^2.
steps.why: Setting x = 4 in y = -(x - 4)^2 yields the maximum value y = 0 at the shifted vertex (4, 0).
